page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ads_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with constrained core counts to benefit workloads requiring substantial memory per CPU core. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7763 processor operating at a clock speed of 3.525 GHz, this x86_64 system provides 4 dedicated virtual CPUs mapped across 2 physical execution cores with simultaneous multithreading. Memory capacity is provisioned at 64.0 GB RAM, delivering an expansive 16.0 GB per vCPU. The instance includes 322 GB of local SSD temporary storage, while hardware graphics acceleration is not present.

Performance benchmarks show a contrast between single-core and parallel multi-core throughput. In stress-ng single-core testing, the instance achieved a strong score of 2702.28, landing in the top 25 percent of tested systems. Conversely, its 4-vCPU ceiling results in weak multi-core scores, including 5399.28 in stress-ng multi-core and 3646.0 in Geekbench multi-core. Large-block uncached memory read bandwidth reached 39.33 GB/sec in the average category, while write bandwidth registered at 22.83 GB/sec. Application testing reflected 4.11 million operations per second on Redis SET tasks and 5.19 GB/sec in static web serving throughput.

The qualitative cost efficiency of the E8-4ads_v5 centers on licensing optimization. By restricting the 8-vCPU E8 chassis down to 4 active vCPUs while retaining the entire 64.0 GB memory pool, users can substantially reduce per-core software licensing expenditures for memory-heavy software. The primary architectural tradeoff is lower aggregate compute parallelism relative to memory size. Consequently, the instance is well suited for memory-intensive caching tiers, enterprise relational databases constrained by per-core database licensing, and in-memory analytical workloads.

This hardware configuration is qualitatively cost-effective for organizations aiming to limit per-core commercial software licensing costs while providing significant memory allocations. The instance fits memory-heavy applications, relational database engines, Redis caching systems, and moderate in-memory processing tasks.
